title: Lifetimes, printed
description:
Watch objects being created and destroyed in different scopes.

```
create A (static)
create B (local in main)
  create C (local in a block)
  destroy C
create D (heap)
destroy D (delete)
destroy B
destroy A
```
hints: Objects in one scope are destroyed in the reverse order they were made (lesson 2.04).
A temporary like `Noisy{"T"}.name.size();` is destroyed at the end of the full expression.
requirements: A `struct Noisy` that prints in its constructor and destructor with its name.
One of each: a static, a local, a local in an inner block, a heap object, and a temporary.
Predict the output in a comment first, then compare.
stretch: Return a `Noisy` from a function and see whether a copy is made (guaranteed elision).
